#7739. The Best Home Thermostats of 2026, Tested and Reviewed

Black Friday Deals Are Already Here ➡️ Tools, Generators, Essentials & More

By Tony Carrick, Paul Rankin, Additional research provided by Glenda Taylor

Published Nov 24, 2026 9:00 AM EST

We may earn revenue from the products available on this page and participate in affiliate programs. Learn More ›

Home thermostats have come a long way from those early models with manual temperature dials that may or may not accurately reflect a room’s actual temperature. Today’s home thermostats are highly efficient. Many are programmable. Some even connect with smart-home systems for remote heating and cooling control via a smartphone app.

We decided to test a variety of home thermostats to see which ones were a step above the rest. Based on our tests, we chose the Google Nest Gen 4 Learning Thermostat as the best overall for its easy installation, adaptive scheduling, and intuitive controls. Keep reading to discover why these models are among the best home thermostats on the market today and to learn which factors to consider when shopping for one of the best home thermostats.

Bottom line: Choosing the right thermostat depends on your needs, from smart features to basic controls. Our top picks cater to various preferences and budgets.

Most shoppers want a home thermostat to have features that help save on utility costs without the device being too complicated. However, the criteria that determine the best home thermostats available today depend on shoppers’ varied wants and needs, according to Michael Morey, senior product manager of thermostats at HVAC manufacturer Trane Technologies based in Davidson, North Carolina. He notes, “The most popular thermostat features include Wi-Fi–enabled remote temperature and humidity control, custom programmable schedules, responsive touch screen with color display, fresh air ventilation control, HVAC system maintenance reminders/alerts, energy savings mode, and over-the-air upgradable software.”

How much a new home thermostat costs typically depends on whether it’s a manual, a programmable, or a smart thermostat. Manual thermostats are the most basic and least expensive models—as low as $20. They usually have an LED screen, a few room temperature buttons, a fan setting, and an AC switch that allows you to set the unit to cool in the summer and heat in the winter.

Choosing a programmable thermostat lets users set heating and cooling schedules based on activity, like having the heat automatically turn on at 6 a.m. on winter weekdays before everyone wakes up.

Smart thermostats allow you to adjust a home’s temperature via an app and include a wide range of features and functions, like occupancy sensing, geofencing, and smart-home integration. These thermostats can cost around $300 or more.

“Programmable thermostats often provide a very basic scheduling functionality, where a smart thermostat provides wider flexibility in scheduling, as well as the ability to make changes on the go,” explains Morey. “Some use geofencing to adjust the temperature when it senses that all a home’s occupants have left and readjust when the occupants are heading back home.”

The best home thermostats must be well made, dependable, and accurate. Any extra features may benefit some users but not others. While these home thermostats vary in features and functions, each one is a quality instrument that will help to reduce heating and cooling costs and is sure to be an asset to any home.

The Google Nest Learning Thermostat notes repetitive tasks—like when the room temperature is usually turned up or down—and adjusts the temperature automatically. Its fourth-generation design pairs a smooth circular dial with a full-color display that users can customize to show temperature information or the day’s weather forecast, complete with animations. It also includes a Nest Temperature Sensor that can be placed in another room to help manage hot and cold spots.

We thought this model felt like a high-quality thermostat, thanks to its premium dial, attractive display, and impressive graphics. Installation was remarkably simple, with clear, app-guided instructions and a thoughtfully designed mounting system. We especially liked setting the display to show the day’s forecast with subtle visual cues, such as animated rainfall. The Google Home app was fast and easy to navigate, making remote temperature adjustments and schedule changes straightforward.

The learning functions are one of the main draws, and they worked well throughout testing. Over time, the thermostat adapted to our temperature habits, adjusting schedules without requiring constant input. We also found the Google Home app fast and easy to navigate, whether making a quick remote adjustment or changing the schedule. Although the Nest costs more than basic competitors, its combination of automation, design, and ease of use made it our best overall pick.

What our tester says: “I’ve tested a lot of smart home gear, but this is one of the few products that feels genuinely joyful to use every single day. From the display to the app, everything just works exactly how you want it to.”—Paul Rankin, Product Reviews tester and writer

Get the Google home thermostat at Amazon, Lowe’s, The Home Depot, or Walmart.

The Amazon smart thermostat doesn’t take up much room, but it still offers high-end smart features. Users can set this programmable thermostat through the touch screen. It offers voice control through select smart-home devices and the Amazon Alexa app and adjusts the temperature based on user preferences to reduce energy usage.

We loved how easy this thermostat was to use. By simply clicking on Climate and the thermostat you want to control in the app, you’re presented with full-screen, color-coded controls that include a slider for adjusting the temperature or heat and cool settings if you have the thermostat set to Auto.

During our testing, we used voice commands to change the temperature or set a schedule via our Echo Show device and found it easy to create and manage a 7-day temperature schedule. A key feature allows Amazon Alexa to automatically change the thermostat settings based on the “hunches” it has about whether the user is home, away, or asleep based on the location of their phone and how they interact with the home’s Alexa devices.

For eco-conscious users, the Amazon thermostat offers energy-tracking features that estimate how much energy the HVAC system is consuming each day. However, while we liked this feature, we wondered about the accuracy of the measurements.

This thermostat features a sleek minimalist appearance that mimics the look of the Amazon Echo Dot. Yet, it still has a large digital display to allow users to easily see the temperature, even from across the room.

Get the Amazon home thermostat at Amazon.

If you’re searching for a basic thermostat, look no further than the Emerson Non-Programmable single-stage thermostat. One button raises the temperature and the other lowers it—from heating to cooling with a simple press of the finger.

This no-frills thermostat is well suited to users who want to set and change the temperature by themselves without the need for programs or a Wi-Fi connection. An easy-to-read LED screen shows the desired room temperature and the current temperature. It doesn’t require a C-wire: Just follow the installation instructions for a relatively simple DIY chore.

During our testing, this thermostat performed its basic job effectively: maintaining the room temperature at a consistent level. The controls are bare bones, but the thermostat does have a backlit display for making nighttime temperature adjustments.

For shoppers looking for a thermostat that does the absolute basics and nothing more, this is an ideal pick.

Get the Emerson home thermostat at Amazon or Lowe’s.

The Honeywell Home T9 Smart Thermostat With Sensor is a good fit for homes where some rooms stay warmer or cooler than others. It combines room-based temperature monitoring, motion detection, and geofencing to help keep occupants comfortable without constant manual adjustments. During testing, we found its controls accurate and intuitive, with the remote sensor providing its biggest advantage over a thermostat that measures temperature only where it’s mounted.

The T9 lets users select which room’s temperature the system should prioritize. We especially appreciated this feature in a cold bonus room, where it helped us raise the temperature without overheating the rest of the house. Choosing a specific room took the guesswork out of sensor-based adjustments and gave us more direct control over comfort. Geofencing also automatically adjusted settings when we were away, helping reduce unnecessary heating and cooling.

The full-color touchscreen clearly displays the current temperature, target temperature, and humidity. We had no trouble changing heating and cooling settings directly on the thermostat, while the Honeywell app made scheduling and remote adjustments straightforward. Installation requires a C-wire, and adding more room sensors increases the cost. Still, for households dealing with uneven temperatures, the T9’s room-prioritization feature makes it a worthwhile upgrade.

Get the Honeywell Home T9 home thermostat at Amazon.

You will easily be able to see the temperature from across the room via the large digital display on the Honeywell Wi-Fi programmable thermostat. The full-color display also shows the date, day, time, outdoor temperature, and indoor and outdoor humidity levels.

During our week of testing, we programmed this smart thermostat to follow a 7-day schedule, which we could do either directly on the display or through the intuitive and easy-to-use app. We could also select an optional energy-saving mode to reduce electricity costs.

The Honeywell thermostat syncs with digital assistants, including Google Home and Amazon Alexa. A C-wire and a home Wi-Fi network are required to operate the thermostat.

We liked the tabs on the touch screen that made it easy to access various settings, set schedules, and even view a weather forecast all with the touch of a finger. You can even change the color scheme on the thermostat.

While we liked this Honeywell smart thermostat, we were disappointed that it lacked key features that are common on most smart thermostats at this price point, namely geofencing functionality and a vacation mode.

Get the Honeywell Home Wi-Fi 9000 home thermostat at Amazon.

The Ecobee Premium Smart Thermostat claims that it will take keeping your home at the optimal temperature to the next level. We did like the interface and app. However, the Ecobee failed to deliver on the extras that are supposed to separate it from more affordable smart thermostats. We were most excited about the sensor that provides air quality reports. However, the thermostat was attempting to calibrate the air quality sensor during the entire testing period—a process that the manual notes should only take 24 hours. More importantly, our testing revealed significant issues with controlling gas furnace temperature: The Ecobee routinely heated the room to 3 to 4 degrees Fahrenheit above the set temperature before finally cutting it off (we verified the actual room temperature through the use of two independent room thermometers). Given these problems and the steep price tag, we’d be hard-pressed to recommend this model.

We looked at 30 different home thermostats to narrow our choices down to the top models on our list. Our selections come from some of the best-known brands in thermostats and cover a broad range of price points, from basic digital models to premium smart thermostats.

We assessed each home thermostat by installing and using each one for about a week. During that testing period, we assessed how well they performed their basic function of controlling a home’s heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) system and maintaining set temperatures. We also used and evaluated any additional features, including schedule programming and, if applicable, smart features like geofencing, auto-scheduling, smartphone apps, and any smart sensors included with the thermostat.

While you might be tempted to run out and buy a smart thermostat that promises energy efficiency, don’t pull out the credit card until you’re sure it’s the right pick for your home. The best home thermostats are compatible with an existing heating and cooling system, offer features to make life simpler, and fit within your budget, which includes allowing for professional installation costs if necessary.

When it comes to choosing the best home thermostat, one size does not fit all. Some thermostats only control heat; some only control cooling, and some control both. The type of thermostat required depends on the HVAC system in the home. To determine the type of thermostat their home needs, shoppers will want to remember:

Smart thermostats may require users to place sensors in various rooms around the home to sense activity, monitor the temperature, and adjust the heating and cooling accordingly. While they add to a thermostat’s expense, Morey says they’re worth it. “Many of the latest smart thermostats offer remote temperature and humidity sensors that can be placed throughout the home,” he explains. “The thermostat can wirelessly connect to these sensors and control the temperature in a home in a way that keeps your comfort consistent throughout the home.” When any of these factors change or deviate from the norm, the sensor will trigger the thermostat to send an alert to the user’s smartphone.

The best home thermostat is easy to see and program. These days, many manual and programmable thermostats feature large LED screen displays and easy-to-follow prompts. These prompts help the user set the room temperature and program a custom heating and cooling schedule directly through the thermostat.

While you can set some smart thermostats much the same way as the manual and programmable varieties, their programming capabilities can be a bit more limited. Many smart thermostats are built with a small screen and require you to program them via an app that you must download and access through a smartphone, tablet, or PC.

Replacing an existing manual or programmable thermostat with a new manual or programmable model is relatively simple: The existing wires simply connect to the new thermostat. Installing this type of thermostat is often a DIY project.

Replacing an existing smart thermostat with a new one may also be a DIY project. However, if a C-wire is not available, running a new one is typically a job for an electrician. Installing the smart thermostat is only the first part of the task. Next, the user must download an app and follow the prompts to connect the thermostat to the home’s Wi-Fi network. Most of the time, this is relatively simple with a basic knowledge of routers and networks.

Thermostats were always meant to be functional, not decorative. While many basic models that lean more toward functionality are still available today, a lot has changed over the years in terms of aesthetics. These days, many thermostats have sleek digital display screens that look more appealing than their older counterparts. Some allow users to download a chosen background image onto the display. Most are low profile, so they don’t stick out far from the wall. A few newer models are even designed for recessing in a wall stud space, making the front of the screen nearly flush with the wall’s surface for a sleek, clean look.

Before upgrading to a new thermostat, many shoppers often have questions about which option they should choose. While some would rather stick to a functional, manual thermostat, others interested in creating cooling and heating schedules want to know more about programmable and smart options. Here are a few of the most frequently asked questions and their answers about the latest thermostats.

Probably, but some additional wiring may be required to install a smart thermostat if the home is more than 5 to 10 years old.

A smart thermostat connects to your home’s Wi-Fi network to relay information and allows you to control the HVAC system remotely or by voice commands.

Yes. Smart thermostats must connect to the Wi-Fi in a home so they can communicate with a smartphone.

Programmable thermostats can be smart or nonsmart. Select one that can schedule at least 7 days of heating and cooling and lets you override the schedule by adjusting the temperature.

Yes, if your home already has a C-wire installed. If your home doesn’t have a C-wire, a professional must install one first.

The features that make the thermostat “smart” (like geofencing and smartphone app control) won’t work when the internet is out, but you can still control the thermostat manually.

Tony Carrick is a freelance writer specializing in home improvement, landscaping, technology, home security, and design. #7737. Can There Be Democratic Socialism Without Wokism?

Mostly law professors | Sometimes contrarian | Often libertarian | Always independent

A Jacobin editor decries the excesses of "Woke I," and warns that it's still here.

Jacobin senior editor Meagan Day takes to the pages of the NYT to decry woke excess, and argue that it need not be a part of democratic socialist politics. Indeed, she fears wokism will "pull the left off course."

To hear many conservatives define it, I would be considered woke. I've been a member of the Democratic Socialists of America for 10 years. I believe this country needs deep criminal justice and police reform. I am galled by ICE agents ethnically profiling and brutalizing people. I not only support gay marriage but am an enthusiastic participant in one.

But wokeness is not about a basic concern for social justice. It hyperfocuses on language and identity, fights dirty from the moral high ground and mandates deference to self-appointed spokespeople for marginalized groups. It conflates disagreement with harm, and keeps careful watch for heretics.

Day's comments are not merely based upon her experience during the Great Awokening, but also as a student at Oberlin where she saw what she calls "Woke Beta." Now she fears wokeness could derail the ability of Democrats to advance socialist priorities.

President Trump's re-election quieted calls to defund and diversify. But wokeness persists today. In D.S.A., which I joined on the heels of the first Bernie Sanders presidential campaign, one still encounters debates about whether clapping is ableist or whether socialists should commit to "decolonizing 'Minnesota.'" At its best, D.S.A. strikes me as our greatest shot at building a broad-based and politically serious organized left. At its worst, the energy reminds me of a scene from an Oberlin dining co-op, where a group of members filed in during a meal and silently unfurled a sign reading, "This co-op is messed up." (They were protesting the privilege inherent in cliques; the sign's wording was in fact less polite.)

The next Congress can't let these debates trickle up again. The freshman representatives from the bluest districts, such as those in Brooklyn and Los Angeles, will still face pressure to spend their time denouncing offensive language and censuring members to their right. Instead, they should focus on making life better for working-class people — working toward Medicare for all, labor law reform, maybe even a Green New Deal. For the first time in a while, the moderate members of their party might actually be open to compromising on these issues.

As for wokeness, I suspect that many progressive elected officials are privately rankled by its excesses, but publicly inclined to ignore it, worried about inviting moral hectoring from the left. The most productive thing they can do now is grow a backbone. They need to take it upon themselves to elevate the best, most compelling ideas even when doing so earns them some pushback.

Day's arguments, including her suggestion that DSA types should embrace "carceral minimalism" instead of prison abolition--what she calls a "nonsensical position"--is facing pushback from the Left. We will see whether the new Democratic majority takes her advice.

You don't need to splash out on a premium tree this Christmas. With a little know-how, you can turn a budget option into something truly special.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

When you take the kids out to choose a Christmas tree, everyone has in mind a lush, deep green, perfectly shaped evergreen that is featured in holiday advertisements. But not every evergreen in the lot has that kind of sex appeal, especially budget trees for sale in grocery stores, supermarkets, and big-box retailers. These affordable trees can look thin, sparse, and like they didn’t get any sleep last night.

But don’t worry, an inexpensive grocery store Christmas tree can be “spruced up” nicely with a few simple tricks. Yes, you can turn ugly ducklings into beautiful centerpieces by taking steps to make a Christmas tree look fuller, well-structured, and fresh. I’ll explain how to make a real Christmas tree look better with Christmas tree care tips that boost your tree's wow-power.

In this guide, I'm going to walk you through the easy steps you can take to improve your tree dramatically, from a sparse Christmas tree to a festive showstopper. And I promise it won’t cost you a fortune.

There are many reasons that a freshly cut Christmas tree can look droopy and sparse in the store. These include transport stress and dehydration. One of the quickest fixes with a big punch is to make a fresh cut on the bottom of the trunk, taking off around ½ inch. A good folding saw, such as the Rexberi 11-Inch Folding Saw from Amazon, will make light work of this, and it's handy for pruning jobs around the garden, too.

Immediately after cutting, pop the tree into a sturdy stand with water. The Krinner Genie Christmas Tree Stand has a foot-pedal mechanism that makes it easy to secure the tree, plus a built-in water reservoir. But it's not cheap, and if you're buying a budget tree, chances are you'll want a budget-friendly stand to go with it. The Leejec Christmas Tree Stand is a good, affordable alternative, with a generous water reservoir and a handy water level indicator.

Don't leave the tree sitting around after making the cut. The cut surface can dry out, reducing moisture uptake, so getting it into water promptly gives it the best chance of staying fresh.

That sorrowful evergreen you brought home needs time to relax. Once you prune off the very bottom of the trunk, set the tree in a bucket of water and give it time to rehydrate. Leave it wrapped in its netting overnight, which will also make it easier to maneuver into its stand the next day.

Sign up for the Gardening Know How newsletter today and receive a free copy of our e-book "How to Grow Delicious Tomatoes".

Once the tree is securely in place, remove the wrapping and let the branches gradually drop and spread into their natural shape for a few hours. You might be surprised how much fuller it looks after a little time to settle.

Now it's time to give your tree a little makeover. Walk around it and look carefully at its shape. There will likely be a few stray or uneven branches that need tidying up, particularly if you've bought a cheaper tree that hasn't been professionally shaped.

To prune your Christmas tree, take a sharp pair of bypass pruners – Fiskars Bypass Pruning Shears from Amazon are a good, affordable option – and start by removing any broken, damaged, or awkwardly protruding branches. Trim back overly long branches to a side shoot where possible, rather than cutting bluntly through the tips.

Pay particular attention to the lower branches. Remove any that drag on the floor or interfere with the stand, making clean cuts close to the trunk without damaging the bark. This will give the tree a neater silhouette and make it easier to reach the water reservoir.

Step back regularly to check your progress, working toward a balanced cone shape without making the tree look unnaturally perfect. Go easy, though – you can always take more off, but you can't put a branch back.

Starting at the bottom of the tree, gently separate any branches that have become compressed during transport. Work your way upward, easing crowded branches apart and encouraging them to spread into their natural positions. Take care not to force stiff branches, as they can snap.

Once you've worked your way around the tree, step back and look for any obvious gaps. You may be able to gently reposition flexible branches to make the tree look fuller, but avoid bending or twisting them into unnatural shapes.

Pay particular attention to the lower branches, spreading them outward where possible to help disguise the trunk and tree stand. Near the top, gently separate crowded branches to create a more balanced, tapered shape. Don't worry about making everything perfectly symmetrical – a little natural irregularity is part of the charm of a real Christmas tree.

Have you ever used hair extensions? Or had a friend who used hair weaving to change the volume of their hair? You can use this same technique to fill in the canopy of your Christmas tree by tucking extra evergreen branches into bare spots. It’s a quick way to give a sparse Christmas tree a fuller figure.

What to use for this type of branch extension? Start with any healthy branches you removed when pruning your tree earlier. You can also use evergreen clippings from your own yard or ask for spare branches from the Christmas tree lot. Choose branches that closely match your tree for the most natural finish, or mix two or three types of evergreen to add depth and texture.

For larger bare patches, try tucking in realistic faux evergreen sprays, like these Hananona pine branches. Cedar and pine sprays work particularly well, blending into the natural foliage while adding extra volume.

Tuck the cut ends in toward the trunk, positioning the foliage to disguise any obvious gaps. Use green floral wire, like this Pauleen wire from Amazon, to secure the stems discreetly to existing branches, making sure they're firmly attached. Step back occasionally to check the overall effect, adding a few more sprigs wherever the tree still looks sparse.

We all have good sides and bad sides, and your Christmas tree might too. If one side is lopsided or less impressive, simply turn it toward the wall. Of course, this trick works less well if you have a revolving tree stand.

Some gaps may still be visible after fluffing up the branches and adding extras, but that's where clever decorating comes to the rescue. Tuck large ornaments deep inside the tree, closer to the trunk, to disguise bare spots and create a sense of depth.

Another great trick is to cluster smaller ornaments in groups of three to make sparse areas look fuller. If one part of the tree is overloaded with decorations, move a few into the gaps to create a more balanced look. You can also use pinecones, artificial flowers, or decorative picks to add texture and interest.

Finally, try weaving wide ribbons or garlands through the branches to disguise any remaining gaps. Rather than wrapping them tightly around the outside, tuck sections deeper into the tree and let them billow outward. This creates the illusion of a much fuller, more luxurious Christmas tree without spending a fortune.

Keeping your tree looking good until Christmas requires a little effort. Here are some top tips:

A healthy cat is a beautiful cat. Okay, that might be a bit of a stretch, but your catâs skin and coat are indeed a window into their overall health.

Skin is the bodyâs largest organ, and signs of poor health and nutritional deficits often show up here before larger problems develop. So when a food supports a lustrous coat and healthy skin, itâs usually good for your catâs overall health as well.

Thatâs the approach Kika USA has taken with their cat food. Their wet and dry food formulas are uniquely designed to meet the demands of the largest organ, using high-protein, high-omega formulas that support not only skin and coat health, but also the immune and digestive systems. Because, in the end, itâs all connected to your kitties' overall health.

I had a chance to try Kika USAâs dry food options, including their White Cats formulaâwith the help of my white cat, Makoaâand their wet food toppers. Keep reading to find out if these unique coat-specific diets are the key to your cat's health and beauty.

Did you know that your catâs skin accounts for about a quarter of their body weight? With that in mind, it should be no surprise that your catâs skin uses an incredible amount of the nutrients they consume, especially protein. In fact, fur is composed of approximately 95% protein, and hair growth and skin renewal can account for roughly 25 to 30% of daily protein requirements.1 Dietary fats are equally important, as essential fatty acids help maintain the skinâs protective barrier and support a soft, supple coat.

Because of this, if your cat isnât getting enough protein, omega fatty acids, and other essential nutrients in their diet, it is often the skin that shows the first signs. A dull, brittle coat, excessive shedding, flaky skin, or hair loss may signal nutritional deficiencies.

The larger problem? Many cat foods on the market donât provide enough protein to meet the needs of the skin and coat, as well as the rest of their body. And even fewer foods provide enough quality fatty acids.

Kika USA grew from a family business started in Lithuania in 1991 by a passionate group of cat and dog show groomers and breeders. They knew how important nutrition is in building a strong, healthy, lustrous coat, and they brought that knowledge to their line of specialty cat and dog foods that would eventually make their way to the US.

These diets prioritize high amounts of quality animal protein, omega fatty acids, and other unique nutrients proven to support skin and coat health. Uniquely, Kika USA offers specific dry food formulas for different coat colors. Their White Cats, Dark Cats, and Red Cats formulas are made with the same base ingredients, but with special attention to specific amino acids and superfoods, including L-tyrosine, L-cysteine, L-tryptophan, dried carrots, and flaxseed.

Together, these ingredients support overall coat health while specific recipe tweaks help maintain coat pigment and reduce staining.

Kika USA is best suited for adult cats over one year old who might benefit from extra support for healthy skin and coat.

The dry food comes in recipes for red, dark, and white coats, making this brand especially useful for cats struggling with pigmentation issues, dullness, and staining.

The wet food range is primarily designed as a supplemental topper for adult cats, adding variety and moisture to regular meals, rather than a complete diet. There is also a kitten formula topper for immune support in younger cats.

Kika USAâs dry cat food formulas feature herring meal as their primary ingredient, providing a concentrated source of animal protein to support muscle maintenance, healthy skin, and coat condition. Poultry fat and salmon oil supply dietary fats, including omega fatty acids that help maintain a soft, glossy coat. Dried eggs offer additional animal-based protein, while ingredients such as flaxseed contribute beneficial fatty acids.

The recipes also include taurine, an essential nutrient for feline heart and eye health, alongside vitamins, minerals, and biotin to support overall wellness.

The majority of the ingredients in Kikaâs recipes are great, but there are some less desirable additions. Pea and potato protein boost the formulasâ overall protein content but provide less species-appropriate nutrition than animal sources. Potatoes and peas in whole form also feature prominently, meaning plant-based ingredients play a substantial role.

Although Kika USA offers separate dry food formulas for red, dark, and white-coated cats, their ingredient lists are remarkably similar. All three feature herring meal as the primary protein, alongside poultry fat, salmon oil, plant-based proteins, and essential vitamins and minerals.

The main differences lie in a few additions and minor variations in guaranteed nutrient levels. The red formula uniquely includes dried carrots, while both the red and dark formulas contain supplemental L-tyrosine, L-cysteine, and L-tryptophanâamino acids involved in various physiological processes, including pigmentation. Studies have shown that insufficient dietary L-tyrosine can cause black cats' fur to turn reddish-brown, while higher dietary concentrations can help maintain black pigmentation.2

The dark and white formulas guarantee slightly more crude protein than the red formula, while the white formula has marginally less crude fat.

Kika USAâs wet food offers adult cats two seafood-based options: tuna and tuna with shrimp. Both feature tuna as the primary ingredient, providing animal-based protein, while the shrimp formula adds another seafood source with unique micronutrients. The recipes also include tuna extract, a small amount of rice, and added ingredients such as taurine and vitamins, depending on the formula.

Their high moisture content can help supplement a catâs daily water intake, while the soft texture and seafood flavors may appeal to picky eaters. Marketed as supplemental toppers, these products are designed to add variety to an existing diet rather than replace a complete and balanced food.

For kittens, Kika USA also offers a tuna-and-sea-bass kitten formula with added vitamin E, vitamin C, and zinc to support a growing catâs nutritional needs.

Kika USA also offers a few supplements that are worth mentioning. These products focus on targeted mineral support for different life stages.

There are three formulas, including a puppy and kitten supplement for bone strength, joint health, and detox, an adult performance formula focused on bone strength and muscle recovery, and a senior formula targeting bone health, neuromuscular balance, and healthy aging.

Kika USA products are available directly through the official Kika USA website, which offers its full range of cat food formulas, wet-food toppers, supplements, and treats. You can also shop online through Petco, Chewy, Amazon, and Walmart.

For in-person shopping, Kika USA is stocked at select Petco stores and grooming salons, though availability varies by location.

This isnât my first encounter with Kika USA. I recently had the opportunity to try their Superior Care White Dogs Grain-Free Small Breed Dog Food, and while my Dalmatian mix was a little larger and "spottier" than their intended clientele, she still enjoyed it. And it is now my friendâs go-to food for her Maltese. So I was very excited to get the opportunity to try the brandâs cat food recipes.

I received bags of the White Cats, Dark Cats, and Red Cats dry food formulas, each of the wet food topper recipes, and their MZG System supplement.

I started my product testing with a deep dive into their recipesâ ingredients. Mostly, I wanted to know if there really was a difference between the three coat color options. As I mentioned in the product breakdown above, there actually are some slight differences.

The Dark and Red formulas have added amino acids proven to affect pigmentation, while the white formula lacks these. The Red formula also contains carrots, though I didnât find any research supporting carrots or beta-carotene influencing pigmentation in cats.

All three formulas contain ingredients to support overall coat health, and compared to the average cat food, they all have high amounts of protein and omega fatty acids. While I am not a huge fan of the inclusion of pea protein, potatoes, or peas, I was happy to see herring meal listed as the first ingredient, as this provides a natural source of those omega fatty acids and plenty of species-appropriate protein.

The wet food options are also made from a fish base, in this case tuna, with some key added ingredients.Taurine ensures cats get enough of this essential amino acid, while added sodium aluminosilicate helps detoxify the gut.

Once I was satisfied that the ingredients were up to snuff, it was time to let Makoa conduct his product tests.

Iâm not sure what specifically it is about this dry food, but Makoa really does seem to love it! True, he is a glutton and has never met a food he didnât like, but he seems especially excited about this dry food, even without the toppers, and attacked all three dry formulas with enthusiasm.

Currently, I am feeding only the White Cats variety, in the hope that it will help improve his tear stains â so far, so good!

Not surprisingly, Makoa is also a big fan of the wet food toppers. I mix a little in with his dinner each night, and he just gobbles it all up. I love that they add moisture and some fun new flavors to his meals, as well as extra protein.

I have also been using the MZG System supplement that came with my review package. This mineral-based supplement is marketed as supporting healthy bones, joints, and teeth, as well as aiding in detoxification.

Makoa happily eats the supplement mixed into his food, and I am hopeful that it will also help to keep his tears clear through those detoxing effects.

Overall, I am a fan of this food. While the differences in formulas might be slight, the ingredients alone are worth the buy. The focus on skin- and coat-supporting ingredients makes them a great option for cats struggling with dull fur, dandruff, and other common coat problems.

Kika USA's wet foods are marketed as toppers, meaning they donât contain everything needed to be a complete meal. They make a great addition to the companyâs dry food or your dry food of choice.

Herring meal is the primary ingredient in Kika USA's dry formulas, providing concentrated animal protein. Poultry fat, salmon oil, and eggs contribute additional nutrients.

Kika USA offers dry formulas tailored to red, dark, and white coats. Their ingredients include nutrients involved in coat health and pigmentation. Each contains protein and omega fatty acids to support healthy skin and lustrous fur, but specific color-enhancing benefits aren't conclusively established.

If your catâs coat is a bit lackluster, the problem may be more than skin deep. The right nutrition is key to providing the protein, omegas, and nutrients your cat needs not just for a healthy coat, but overall health.

Kika USA dry food, wet food toppers, and supplements put skin and coat health first, knowing everything else will follow. Their coat-color-specific formulas offer key amino acids for pigmentation and detoxing, while their base ingredients offer the protein and fats your cat craves and needs to thrive.

#7732. Florida Law Allowing Bar Liability for Knowingly Serving "Habitually Addicted" Doesn't Apply When Server Only Saw One Drinking Session

Mostly law professors | Sometimes contrarian | Often libertarian | Always independent

From Croteau v. Family 5, Inc., decided Wednesday by Florida Court of Appeal Chief Judge Jonathan Gerber, joined by Judges Marlon Weiss and Johnathan Lott:

In this personal injury case, the plaintiff appeals from the circuit court's final summary judgment which found … that the plaintiff could not prove her negligence action against a bar which had served her alcoholic beverages before she was injured later that night. The summary judgment rested on the circuit court's application of "the dram shop statute"—section 768.125, Florida Statutes (2020):

Liability for injury or damage resulting from intoxication. A person who sells or furnishes alcoholic beverages to a person of lawful drinking age shall not thereby become liable for injury or damage caused by or resulting from the intoxication of such person, except that a person who willfully and unlawfully sells or furnishes alcoholic beverages to a person who is not of lawful drinking age or who knowingly serves a person habitually addicted to the use of any or all alcoholic beverages may become liable for injury or damage caused by or resulting from the intoxication of such minor or person.

The underlined second exception is at issue here…. In addressing "what constitutes 'knowledge' in order for a vendor's conduct to be found negligent," the [Florida Supreme Court has] found:

[T]he cause of action [under section 768.125's second exception] only requires evidence that the vendor had knowledge that the individual the vendor served was a habitual drunkard. Serving an individual multiple drinks on one occasion would be insufficient, in and of itself, to establish that the vendor knowingly served a habitual drunkard alcoholic beverages. On the other hand, serving an individual a substantial number of drinks on multiple occasions would be circumstantial evidence to be considered by the jury in determining whether the vendor knew that the person was a habitual drunkard….

[In another case,] we affirmed a summary judgment for the defendant bar, where the plaintiff patron was unknown to the bar's staff, was not a bar regular, and had purchased up to four drinks over two to three hours. We held that we could not impute notice of the patron's alcohol addiction to the bar when the patron had not shown any signs of intoxication, despite his alcohol consumption ….

Here, consistent with [those precedents], the bar's serving the alcoholic beverages to the plaintiff for the first time on the incident date, without more, should not be considered sufficient evidence to impute knowledge to the bar that the plaintiff was "habitually addicted to the use of any or all alcoholic beverages." …

Roster v. Moulton (Fla. App. 1992)—the primary case upon which the plaintiff relies—is distinguishable….

[In Roster,] [i]t is undisputed that [the patron] consumed 8–10, 12–ounce cans of beer and two straight shots of tequila over the period of an hour and a half. After a short absence from [the bar], during which [the patron] drank yet another beer served elsewhere, [the patron] returned to [the bar's] walk-up window, where he ordered and was served another beer. The [bar manager] admitted that it would be unusual for a person to consume that many beers and two shots of tequila without showing signs of intoxication. Despite [the patron's] considerable alcohol consumption, [the patron] did not stagger and did not slur his speech. The manager twice asked [the patron] to leave the bar only because [the patron] became loud and argumentative. [The patron] pled guilty to the charge of driving while under the influence of alcohol and admitted that he had a drinking problem from the age of sixteen, which he still had at the time of the accident. At that time, [the patron] had never received treatment for his alcohol addiction….

By affidavit in Roster, "two experts[] … essentially stated that the large amount of alcohol that [the patron had] consumed over a relatively short time period, together with the lack of impairment [which the patron had] demonstrated, would have put a reasonable server of alcohol on notice that [the patron] was habitually addicted to alcohol. [The bar] submitted no affidavits to oppose these viewpoints." …

However, unlike in Roster, as the bar's answer brief submits:

… [W]hatever alcohol [the plaintiff] may have consumed at [the bar], she claims she drank over a five-hour period—much longer than the 90 minutes during which the Roster [patron] consumed 10–12 drinks. Furthermore, [the plaintiff] claims she sat, ordered drink(s), and watched television for five hours, which is much different than the Roster [patron,] who left the bar …, drank another alcoholic beverage elsewhere, and then came back to the bar where he was served yet another drink. Also, unlike … in Roster, there is no evidence that [the plaintiff] demonstrated a level of intoxication consistent with someone who had either a high or low tolerance for alcohol. Finally, unlike the [patron] in Roster, [the plaintiff here] did not become loud or argumentative at the [bar]. By her own admission, she was quiet, not boisterous, not loud, not abusive, and she simply kept to herself….

Unlike the Roster patron, the plaintiff here was an anonymous patron, whose behavior during her visit to the bar was, by her own statements, unremarkable.

Judge Lott agreed, but added that he thought Roster was wrongly decided, including in its reliance on expert evidence:

Section 768.125, Florida Statutes (2020), says that a bar owner is not liable for damage caused by the sale of alcoholic beverages, except that (as relevant here) a person "who knowingly serves a person habitually addicted to the use of any or all alcoholic beverages may become liable." The language does not require expert testimony, and does not ask how the latest version of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM) defines pathologies related to alcohol use….

The statutory language asks whether the server has actual knowledge that the person is, as a matter of habit, addicted to alcohol…. You know such a thing when you see it—and it's hard to imagine being able to see it given only a single occasion of indulgence…. [A]nyone can have too many drinks. What separates a "habitual drunkard" [which is how the concurrence elsewhere interprets "habitually addicted"] is that the habitual drunkard feels compelled to do so on account of their addiction, and does so regularly as a matter of habit….

Turning back to Roster—where was the evidence that the defendant actually knew that the plaintiff was habitually addicted to alcohol? The defendant observed the plaintiff drink heavily on one occasion wherein he handled his liquor well, until he didn't. No evidence of "addiction" was presented, much less of a "habit" of it. The expert affidavits about his apparent alcohol tolerance added nothing to that inquiry.

In sum, Roster passed the buck from the statutory language to expert opinion, and reached the wrong result in turn. In an appropriate case, we should consider whether to recede from it….

Jack R. Reiter and Robert C. Weill (GrayRobinson, P.A.) represent the bar.

Eugene Volokh is the Thomas M. Siebel Senior Fellow at the Hoover Institution at Stanford, and the Gary T. Schwartz Distinguished Professor of Law Emeritus and Distinguished Research Professor at UCLA School of Law. #7731. 70+ Dogs Rescued From South Korean Meat Farm as 2027 Ban Approaches

We just sent a welcome email your way with a quick overview of what to expect (including those vital recall alerts).

Nearly 30 dogs have arrived in New York after being rescued from a dog-meat farm in South Korea. Their journey toward adoption is beginning, but with the country's ban still months away from taking full effect, the work is far from over.

A plane ride to New York probably wasn't on these dogs' bingo cards. Neither, for that matter, was a soft bed, a full bowl of food, or the chance to be someone's beloved family member. After spending their lives confined to cages, even the simplest things may seem exciting and new.

On October 1, nearly 30 dogs were rescued from a dog-meat farm in Gangjin, South Korea, that once bred and slaughtered as many as 1,000 dogs each year. This was part of a larger rescue operation by Humane World for Animals that saved more than 70 dogs from the property.

For the organization, the operation marks its final large-scale dog-meat-farm rescue in South Korea ahead of the country's ban, which takes full effect on February 7, 2027. Humane World for Animals has rescued nearly 3,000 dogs from farms since 2015, making this a significant milestone.

And yes, it's a reason to celebrate. But before we get too comfortable patting ourselves on the back, there's a much bigger picture to consider. Getting these dogs out was a huge victory, but there are still thousands at risk.

When the rescue team arrived at the farm in Gangjin, in South Korea's South Jeolla Province, they were met with disturbing scenes. Rows of rusting cages, abandoned collars scattered on the ground, and skeletal remains served as a gruesome reminder of the dogs that hadn't been so lucky.

It's a hard reality to come to terms with, especially if your own dog is currently hogging the sofa, demanding snacks, or staring at you as though you've ruined their life by being five minutes late with dinner. The minor dramas faced by our beloved pets are a world away from what these poor dogs endured.

Humane World for Animals has reported finding mixed breeds and dogs of different sizes during its rescue work. The survivors included Jindos, a breed native to South Korea, a husky mix, and smaller dogs, including a spitz mix. In other words, any dog could end up on the menu.

In this most recent rescue, a concerned citizen alerted a local animal protection group, which contacted Humane World for Animals and the authorities. Officials found that the farm had broken South Korea's Animal Protection Act. The farmer, a man in his 80s, agreed to hand over the dogs and promised not to take part in the dog-meat trade again.

More than 70 dogs were rescued. Nearly 30 travelled to New York, another 12 went to a rehabilitation center in Montreal, and some mothers and their puppies remained in South Korea because they were too young to fly safely.

Rescuing dogs from situations like this isn't as simple as just opening a cage and booking the next available flight. International transport requires veterinary checks, vaccinations, documentation, and careful consideration about which animals are fit to travel. The priority is getting them out safely, not rushing them onto a plane for the sake of a happy headline.

South Korea passed its Special Act on the Termination of Breeding, Slaughter, and Distribution of Dogs for Consumption in January 2024. Its key prohibitions will finally take full effect on February 7, 2027, making it illegal to breed, slaughter, or sell dogs or dog meat for human consumption. But the transition is already underway.

In May 2026, South Korea's Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs reported that about 82% of the country's 1,537 registered dog-meat farms had closed. Over a thousand farms closed is something worth celebrating, but it means 272 farms are still operating.

Another consideration is that closing a farm doesn't automatically save the dogs living there. A business can shut down, the gates can close, and the paperwork can be signed, but where do all those dogs go?

According to Humane World for Animals, government figures indicate that of approximately 393,857 dogs counted on farms that had been closed, only 1,121 were adopted or transferred to public shelters. That's about 0.3%.

Itâs understood that most of these dogs were sent for slaughter or moved to other farms. So, while the closure of dog meat farms is good news, itâs not a true victory if these dogs are simply moved on to face the same fate. The ban is a huge step forward, but a law is only as good as its enforcement.

The real goal isn't just to close the farms. It's making sure the dogs are actually safe.

Getting out of the farm is the first big hurdle for these dogs. Now comes veterinary care, recovery, and the not-so-small task of learning how to live in a completely different world.

Humane World for Animalsâ rescue protocols include veterinary exams, vaccinations, respiratory screening when needed, and the health documents required for international travel. Each dog has their own needs. Some may need treatment for skin problems, wounds, dental disease, or nutritional deficiencies.

The second, and perhaps most challenging, hurdle for these dogs is adapting to a whole new way of life. Just because a dog has been saved doesn't automatically mean a dog feels safe.

Imagine never having lived in a home, then suddenly finding yourself surrounded by doors, stairs, strange noises, slippery floors, and humans who keep trying to show you how much they love you. Even a well-meaning hug could be overwhelming. And the vacuum cleaner? Let's just say it probably won't be winning any popularity contests.

These dogs may need to learn things many pets take for granted: how to explore a room, relax around people, or understand that a hand reaching toward them isn't something to fear. Some will be curious from the start. Others may prefer to watch from a safe distance. Neither response is wrong, and patience plus a little common sense go a long way.

A quiet place to rest, a predictable routine, and the freedom to explore without being pushed can help a dog settle in. Rewarding small steps with positive reinforcement builds confidence without turning every new experience into a test.

Adjusting to a new life takes time, and there's no need to rush it. A dog who hides under the table on day one isn't a failed adoption. A dog who isn't ready for cuddles isn't being ungrateful. Theyâre figuring things out, and they need time to decide that this strange new place might actually be safe. Building trust and confidence can be a slow process.

Those familiar with the process of adopting or fostering dogs, particularly those who may not have had the best start to life, may have heard of the 3-3-3 Rule for Dogs: 3 days, 3 weeks, 3 months. Itâs a simplified interpretation of the timeline many dogs tend to follow when adjusting to a new home environment.

The first 3 days are about decompression and resetting the nervous system. It might look like a dog that is timid, constantly moving, hiding, or even showing signs of aggression. Some dogs adjust quickly, while others may take a little longer than 3 days. The important thing to know is that this version of the dog is not usually a good representation of their true selves.

Over the first 3 weeks, dogs will start to gain confidence and explore their new world. They are often testing boundaries, becoming familiar with patterns, and learning how to trust. Being consistent and providing predictable routines is paramount to this process.

By the time 3 months have passed, most dogs will be feeling more settled. It may still take some time for their full personality to appear, but with every passing month, they become more confident, more trusting, and less anxious.

Sometimes progress looks like taking a treat from someone's hand. Sometimes it's finally falling asleep without startling at every sound. Those moments might not make a flashy before-and-after video, but for that dog, they're a big deal.

One more thing: fear and behavioural changes shouldn't automatically be dismissed as consequences of a dog's past. Pain, illness, and other medical problems can affect behaviour, too. If a dog seems persistently distressed or suddenly starts acting differently, a veterinary check is important. We don't want to assume it's trauma when there may be pain due to a treatable medical issue behind it.

A second chance isn't just getting a dog out of a cage. It's giving them the medical care, space, and time to discover that life can be safe, and maybe even pretty wonderful.

Humane World for Animals calls the Gangjin operation its final large-scale dog-meat-farm rescue in South Korea. But that doesn't mean the work is over. The organization plans to continue monitoring the ban and supporting efforts to enforce it.

Closing farms is a huge win. Full stop. But making sure dogs aren't left behind, moved elsewhere, or subjected to illegal practices is part of making that win count. With the ban taking full effect in February 2027, the coming months will be crucial.

For the dogs already rescued, a new life is finally within reach. Veterinary care. Rehabilitation. A chance to find a home where the biggest worry is whether they get the good spot on the sofa. That's quite the upgrade.

Now, we turn our attention to the dogs still waiting in South Koreaâs remaining farms. Stopping the dog meat trade is a huge victory, but in many ways, itâs just the beginning. Saving these dogs is more than just stopping the slaughter. Itâs making sure they all get the happy ending they deserve.

#7730. The Best Dual Coffee Makers of 2026, Tested and Reviewed

Black Friday Deals Are Already Here ➡️ Tools, Generators, Essentials & More

By Tony Carrick, Additional research provided by Savannah Sher

Published Nov 24, 2026 9:30 AM EST

We may earn revenue from the products available on this page and participate in affiliate programs. Learn More ›

Dual coffee makers, also known as two-in-one or two-way coffee makers, typically produce full carafes of coffee along with single servings of drip coffee, instant coffee, espresso, and tea. They’re the ideal appliances for households with a variety of coffee preferences.

While choosing the best dual coffee maker might seem like a simple decision, there are actually a number of considerations to weigh. We’ve tested some of the top dual coffee makers on the market and reviewed them here so you can choose the ideal machine to fulfill your daily coffee fix. Our top choice was the Cuisinart Coffee Center 4-in-1 Barista Bar, but there are plenty of options to suit your coffee brewing needs.Read on for reviews of the best coffee makers available today.

Bottom line: Explore the best dual coffee makers of 2026, offering options for every budget and preference, from versatile all-in-one models to specialized espresso machines.

These top picks take into account key shopping considerations for the best dual coffee maker in addition to overall quality and value. Read on to discover some of the top-rated options on the market in a variety of categories for delicious coffee every time.

The versatility of this multifunctional barista bar helped it earn our top spot. Cuisinart’s Coffee Center is a great option for those who enjoy a variety of brews, from morning coffee to a pick-me-up cappuccino or espresso in the afternoon. It comes equipped with a standard 12-cup coffee maker on one side and a single-service brewer on the other. There’s also a steam wand that froths milk for cappuccinos, lattes, and the like.

Not only does it boast two separate reservoirs, one for the standard coffee maker and one for barista-style beverages, it has the ability to steam milk for a latte while simultaneously brewing a full pot of coffee. The single-service side works with 6-ounce, 8-ounce, and 10-ounce capsules, which means it can take both Nespresso capsules and Keurig K-cups.

In testing, we found that the control knob design makes it easy to toggle through and select from different brewing options. But we did have one gripe: The steam wand extended a little low for our usage; we had to search for a glass small enough to fit underneath it so we could froth our milk.

Cleaning the Cuisinart is similar to other dual coffee makers. We liked that most of the removable parts are dishwasher-safe, eliminating the need to hand-wash. While we appreciated the clean feature on the control panel, we’re not sure it’s much different from pressing the “Brew” button. The Cuisinart is one of the larger dual-function coffee makers we tested. While it certainly offers space savings over a Nespresso or Keurig machine and coffee maker, it does take up a fair amount of real estate on the countertop. Still, that larger size is worth it given the versatility it offers.

What our tester says: “As for taste, the coffee-maker side produces robust flavors, especially when engaging the “Bold” option on the control panel. We tried both types of capsules in the single-serve side and found them to be comparable in flavor to the Nespresso and Keurig machines we tested.”—Tony Carrick, Product Reviews tester and writer

Get the Cuisinart Coffee Center 4-in-1 dual coffee maker at Amazon or Wayfair.

Ninja’s specialty coffee maker is one of the most versatile products on the market, capable of brewing a full glass carafe of drip coffee as well as iced coffee and concentrated espresso-style drinks. The built-in milk frother allows you to heat milk and create silky foam for lattes, cappuccinos, and more.

Flavor and serving size options abound with this machine. Use the brew strength control feature to choose between three settings (classic brew, rich brew, super-rich brew) and then select from six brew sizes—single cup, XL single cup, travel mug, XL travel mug, half carafe, and full 10-cup carafe.

All these options could make setting up the Ninja confusing, especially when your brain is still trying to wake up. Luckily, Ninja makes the process easy thanks to a handy double-ended scoop that clearly labels the amount of grounds to add to the filter and a water reservoir with clear markings for each serving size option. The measuring spoon attaches to the side of the machine so it won’t get lost. The reservoir on the Ninja is also a bit shorter than on other dual coffee makers we tested, which makes it easier to fit under the fridge water dispenser to fill with filtered water.

The labeled control knob on the front of the unit makes it easy to dial in the desired size. There are also separate buttons for normal brewing, rich brew, iced coffee, and specialty 4-ounce espresso-style drinks. A built-in steaming wand folds out from the side of the machine for frothing milk.

We found that the Ninja makes a strong, good-tasting brew, especially when using the “Rich” setting. The frother is a nice addition but, unlike with some models we tested, milk must be frothed manually by holding a cup of milk under the wand. This requires a bit more effort to create a cappuccino, latte, or some other specialty drink.

Overall, the Ninja is an excellent and surprisingly affordable choice for anyone who wants to brew coffee as well as a variety of other types of coffee drinks.

Get the Ninja CM401 dual coffee maker at Amazon.

Dual coffee makers tend to be pricier than standard drip coffee makers. However, this Hamilton Beach model boasts both a 12-cup carafe of coffee and single servings at an affordable price. The single-serve function brews up to 14 ounces of coffee, but it uses grounds rather than pods.

The two brewing options are separate (each with their own reservoirs), a setup that lets you brew a single serving while the carafe stays in place. This is useful in households with both coffee drinkers who are on the go and those who work from home. A switch on the control panel makes it easy to toggle between single serving and carafe.

This Hamilton Beach machine isn’t as flashy as some higher-priced models that take K-cups or Nespresso cups, and it doesn’t make cappuccinos or lattes. It does, however, boast some useful additional features, including a 24-hour timer, auto shutoff, and brew pausing. There’s also a brew strength selector that allows coffee drinkers to choose between regular and bold flavors.Though it may lack the bells and whistles of other machines, the budget-friendly Hamilton Beach dual coffee maker is a great choice for those who want the option to brew full pots and single servings.

Get the Hamilton Beach dual coffee maker at Amazon or Best Buy.

When a plain cup of Joe just won’t cut it, Nespresso’s Lattissima One is a premium option to brew espresso, cappuccinos, and other specialty coffee drinks. While a number of machines perform these functions for far less money, the Lattissima makes brewing these barista-style beverages much easier. Simply fill the small milk container to suit the size of cappuccino or latte desired and press the frothing button. About a minute or two later, the specialty coffee drink, complete with a good head of milk froth on the top, is ready to enjoy. There’s no need to hold milk under a frother or even spoon the froth on the drink. The Lattissima does it all automatically.

With loads of Nespresso flavors to choose from (the Lattissima comes with a large sample pack), coffee fans have plenty of options when it comes to the strength and flavor of specialty drinks. Yet while we love how the Lattissima takes the effort out of brewing, the machine cannot brew more than one drink at a time, and it doesn’t make regular coffee. That said, given that the Lattissima is compact at just about 6 inches wide by 13 inches deep, it’s certainly possible to pair it with a traditional coffee machine on a kitchen counter.

Get the Nespresso dual coffee maker at Amazon.

This dual coffee maker brews a full 12-cup glass carafe on one side and single-serving pods on the other. Various aspects of this Cuisinart’s design impressed us in testing. We liked that each side has its own reservoir, so users needn’t empty and refill the reservoir when switching from one brewing mode to the other. We also liked the labeled buttons on the front of the machine that make it a breeze to choose between pods and/or carafe. There’s a control to adjust the temperature of the carafe, which is ideal for those who may not like steaming hot coffee.

In terms of taste, we appreciated the brew strength controls. We found that this machine made rich, flavorful coffee, especially when engaging the “Bold” button. There’s also a button for pausing the coffee maker, which is ideal for grabbing a quick cup mid-brew. For those who want a single serving from coffee grounds as opposed to K-cups, the Coffee Center includes a special single-serving coffee filter that fits into the K-cup holder. With its Extreme Brew feature, we also found that the Cuisinart brews a full carafe more quickly than other coffee makers.

This coffee maker also purports to create iced coffee with its “Over Ice” button, but unfortunately in testing it failed to work properly—the coffee still came out quite hot. Aside from this issue, we found the Cuisinart 2-in-1 coffee maker to be a great option for those who like to switch between K-cups and a full carafe.

Get the Cuisinart Coffee Center 2-in-1 coffee maker at Amazon or Best Buy.

We researched models from the top coffee maker brands and selected and tested those with high customer satisfaction. The selection process factored in brew capacity and sizes, functionality, and special features. Each coffee maker in our lineup comes with a carafe and produces a maximum of 10 or 12 cups of coffee.

Most of the top picks offer two or more brew strengths to accommodate different personal preferences. Select options have a built-in milk frother and accept K-cups or pods. The majority of the coffee makers on the list feature durable stainless steel components for longevity. Some models come with a charcoal filter that enhances flavor, 24-hour programmability, brew pausing, and auto shutoff.

Once assembled, we conducted side-by-side testing of each coffee maker. We considered how easy each machine was to set up, how quickly it brewed coffee, and, of course, the flavor of the finished product. Since these are dual coffee makers, we also tested all of their functions, including their ability to operate as a traditional coffee maker, brew cappuccinos and lattes, and brew with Nespresso cups and Keurig cups.

While it’s easy to assume that all dual coffee makers offer similar performance, several factors affect their functionality, including brew options, size, capacity, carafe type, programmable settings, availability of additional features, and more. Keep reading to learn about several of the most important features to consider when choosing the best dual coffee maker for your kitchen.

Dual coffee makers differ in the types of beverages they produce. Most brew a full carafe of coffee and single-serve coffee, boiling water for hot beverages, and espresso for crafting lattes and cappuccinos. Some models accept coffee pods, while others use ground coffee.

Grind-and-brew coffee makers provided added convenience for those who want freshly ground coffee. When choosing a dual coffee maker with a built-in grinder, look for a model that uses burrs rather than blades. Burrs produce a more consistent grind and generate less heat, so the flavor of the coffee isn’t diminished.

Consider the kitchen’s available countertop space and how much coffee each household member consumes daily. Given their multifunctionality, some dual coffee makers are quite large, taking up approximately 1 square foot of counter space.

Coffee-maker capacity is measured in cups. Keep in mind that “cup” measurements provided by coffee machine manufacturers don’t necessarily align with the standard unit of measurement. A standard U.S. cup measures 8 ounces, while a “cup” from a coffee maker may only measure 4 to 6 ounces.

Coffee makers usually feature either a glass or a thermal carafe, which use different methods to keep coffee warm.

Some dual coffee makers don’t feature a carafe at all, instead dispensing coffee directly into a mug.

Dual coffee makers generally have a variety of programmable settings.

Standard coffee makers typically feature several removable parts that must be cleaned regularly, including the carafe, filter basket, and reusable filter. Dual coffee makers tend to feature even more complex makeups due to their advanced functionality. Look for a model with minimal parts that you can easily assemble and disassemble for cleaning. Those prioritizing ease of cleaning will also want to consider dual coffee makers with dishwasher-safe parts.

Dual coffee makers offer a variety of additional features.

Not quite ready to start brewing? Check out the answers to some of the most frequently asked questions about dual coffee makers.

Dual brew coffee makers vary in their functionality. Most produce a full carafe of drip coffee as well as espresso; single-serve coffee; and boiling water for instant coffee, tea, and cocoa.

Some dual coffee makers, but not all, feature grinders.

Look for a coffee maker with a capacity that suits your household’s needs and brews the type of coffee you enjoy most.

#7728. Better a Bald Head Than a Cat That’s Dead: This Common Hair Growth Formula Is Killing Pets

Catster is reader-supported. When you buy via links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission at no cost to you. Learn more.

Humans have a rather complex and contradictory relationship with their hair. Many of us willingly put ourselves through torturous procedures to remove it from our legs, armpits, and just about anywhere else, while, at the same time, the quest to keep a full and lustrous head of hair fuels a billion-dollar hair growth industry. Since the 1980s, a chemical called Minoxidil has become increasingly popular as both a topical and oral treatment for baldness, but what few people realize is that the very product promising hair growth poses a serious risk to their pets. The American Academy of Dermatology (AAD) is warning consumers about minoxidil toxicity in cats and dogs, highlighting a danger that deserves considerably more attention.

Anyone who shares a home with a cat knows that personal space is more of a suggestion than a household rule. Cats rub against our heads, groom our hair, curl up on our pillows, and somehow manage to investigate just about everything we touch. These perfectly normal feline behaviors can turn deadly when minoxidil enters the picture.

The history of minoxidil shares similarities with another well-known human drug: Viagra, which essentially took a common side effect of the heart medication, sildenafil, and turned it into its primary purpose. In the 1970s, researchers developing a new blood pressure medication found that a common side effect of the drug, minoxidil, was hypertrichosis, aka excessive hair growth. Like the story of sildenafil, the makers of minoxidil leaned into this side effect, repurposing the drug as a treatment for hair loss.1

In 1988, the FDA officially approved minoxidil, and it quickly gained popularity in products like Rogaine. Minoxidil works by widening blood vessels, a process called vasodilation, and altering the hair growth cycle to stimulate hair growth. But what helps us fight hair loss can be dangerous for our feline roommates.

A 2021 study published in the Journal of the American Animal Hospital Association examined 211 reported cases of topical minoxidil exposure in dogs and cats. Of the 87 animals that developed signs of poisoning, 62 were cats, and 25 were dogs. Eight cats died. A 2025 review in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology identified another 94 reported cases, including 68 cats, ten of which died. Notably, 55 of 57 cases involving accidental exposure to a person's minoxidil treatment involved cats.

How does this happen? Topical minoxidil is applied directly to the scalp, either as a liquid using a dropper or as a foam spread with the fingers. Medication can remain on the hands, hair, or nearby surfaces. Cats don't need to break into the medicine cabinet; a little grooming, an affectionate head rub, or a snooze on a contaminated pillow may be enough to expose them. Some were even exposed through everyday contact with their follicle-challenged cat parents.

Minoxidil works by relaxing blood vessels and improving blood flow. In cats, however, the effects can become dangerously disruptive.

When absorbed, it can cause blood pressure to drop dramatically, a condition called hypotension. To compensate, the heart beats faster, but this doesn't necessarily solve the problem. Serious complications can follow, including fluid accumulation in the lungs (pulmonary edema) or in the space surrounding them (pleural effusion). Breathing becomes increasingly difficult, and severe poisoning can progress to cardiovascular and respiratory failure.

Now, what should you look out for? You might notice unusual tiredness, weakness, vomiting, or a sudden loss of appetite. More concerningly, your kitty may start breathing faster than usual or appear to struggle for air. And here's the tricky part: some cats may initially seem perfectly fine.

That's why a suspected exposure should never be brushed off simply because your cat appears normal. Waiting for visible signs of poisoning can waste valuable time.

Now that we are beginning to appreciate the risks this product poses to our pets, we have to wonder how many unexplained cat and dog deaths could be attributed to unknown minoxidil exposure.

Rapunzel may have had a tower to keep her hair safe, but cat owners need a different strategy: keeping minoxidil well away from curious paws.

If you use topical minoxidil, make sure you apply it in a room your cat cannot access. Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water immediately afterward, and clean up any spills promptly. Used tissues, cotton pads, applicators, and empty containers should go straight into a secure bin. That tissue you casually leave on the bathroom counter? To your cat, it might look like just another interesting thing to investigate.

And what about bedtime? If you apply minoxidil in your bedroom, make closing the door part of your nighttime routine. Your cat may protest being left out of the bedroom, especially if your pillow is their favorite sleeping spot, but keeping them away from treated hair, skin, pillows, and bedding can help prevent accidental contact with medication residue. Remember, allowing the product to dry does not guarantee that every surface is free from contamination.

You might be wondering whether switching to oral minoxidil would solve the problem. Unfortunately, not entirely. Oral minoxidil is also toxic to cats if they accidentally ingest a tablet. Whichever formulation you use, keep the medication securely stored and well out of paws' reach. Or better yet, look into options that donât put your pet at risk.

Discuss your household's furry residents with the prescribing dermatologist and establish a routine that prevents accidental exposure. Cats are wonderfully persistent creatures. They may not appreciate a closed door or understand why their favorite pillow is suddenly off-limits, but a little inconvenience is a small price to pay for keeping them safe.

If your cat licks minoxidil, contacts a spill, or may have groomed contaminated fur, contact your veterinarian or an animal poison control service immediately, even if your kitty seems perfectly fine.

Treatment depends on the exposure and your cat's condition. It may involve hospitalization, cardiovascular monitoring, oxygen therapy, intravenous support, and medications to manage complications such as low blood pressure or fluid accumulation.

Never attempt to induce vomiting or administer home remedies unless specifically instructed by a veterinary professional. If medication is still on your cat's coat or skin, ask your veterinarian how to handle decontamination safely rather than delaying emergency care.

Unfortunately, not every cat survives minoxidil poisoning, making every accidental exposure a veterinary emergency.

hhttps://www.instagram.com/reel/DeF7upKOC-1/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&dmpr=NTc4MTIwNjQ2YQ==

Hair loss can affect confidence, and wanting to treat it is perfectly understandable. Minoxidil can be a valuable treatment for people experiencing certain types of hair loss, but sharing a home with a cat adds an important responsibility.

Preventing accidental poisoning starts with awareness. As pet parents, we need to be mindful of the products we bring into our homes, even those that seem perfectly harmless to us. From seemingly innocent houseplants and everyday foods to cleaning products, medications, and personal care treatments, many things we use routinely can pose risks to our feline companions. Before introducing something new into your home, take a moment to consider whether it is safe for your cat. A little research and a few precautions can make a world of difference.

Cats will continue doing what cats do best: following their humans, investigating everything, claiming the pillows, and showing affection on their own terms. We cannot expect them to understand why a particular patch of skin or a freshly treated pillow is suddenly off-limits. That responsibility belongs to us.

Thinning hair can be frustrating, even damaging to self-esteem, but itâs not a life-threatening condition. Losing a beloved pet to an avoidable medication exposure is a tragedy no one should have to experience.

Better bald than catless. Every single time.
